text: The developer tool for Designers Onlook is a free, local-first editor where designers craft exceptional experiences in code → Download today 👨‍💻👩‍💻👨‍💻 We're hiring engineers and designers in SF! 👩‍💻👨‍💻👩‍💻 中文 | Español | Deutsch | français | Português | Русский | 日本語 | 한국어 Craft websites, prototypes, and designs with AI on a canvas built for creative work. See your real app running live, shape it visually, and let your own agent write the code. An open-source alternative to Figma, V0, Replit Agent, Base 44, Webflow, etc. 🖥️ Download the Desktop App (Recommended) – The fastest way to get started with Onlook. 🧑‍💻 Build from source – SOURCE_BUILD.md covers building and running Onlook on a Mac. No Onlook account or cloud keys needed. Because Onlook runs your project with its own tooling, it works with all web frameworks or languages your dev server already supports. If you have a suggestion that would make this better, please fork the repo and create a pull request. You can also browse open issues . See the CONTRIBUTING.md for instructions and code of conduct. To report a security issue, follow SECURITY.md instead of opening a public issue. Onlook collects product usage analytics to help us improve the app. In the official download they are on by default; a build from source asks first. You can turn them off in Settings, or set STUDIO_TELEMETRY=0 to run or build without them. See the privacy policy for details. Onlook's source code is distributed under the Apache 2.0 License. See LICENSE for details. The license covers source code, not every asset in this repository. Onlook's icons come from Central Icons by Iconists. They are licensed to Onlook for its own product, and that license does not extend to forks. Onlook's brand marks, DMG art, and sounds aren't covered either. See ASSETS.md for what's covered and what to replace if you fork, and NOTICE for third-party notices.
